rationale: This is essentially the sign-flipped twin of the archived PeakMarginCapacityExtrapolation (same TS_RANK(capx/at,5) gate, same margin-TS_RANK vs R&D-intensity contrast with the bracket order reversed and the R&D term changed from level to delta), so it is a cosmetic variant rather than a new mechanism.

The R&D-increase × (sales growth minus inventory-intensity build) construction is internally consistent and not directly duplicated in the archive, though the positive loading on raw sales growth cuts against the well-known sales/asset-growth anomaly and the mechanism is close in spirit to the existing inventory-vs-margin family.

Near-duplicate of the archived CapacityBuildDemandOptionGap — identical DELTA(ppegt/at) gate and identical NEG R&D-trend term, with the sales-productivity trend merely re-expressed as cogs growth minus sales growth — and the unnormalized SUMRANK-minus-RANK bracket creates an arbitrary scale/level offset.

The bracket mixes a two-term SUMRANK against a single RANK, leaving a large positive mean offset so that the product is dominated by RANK(aqc/at) itself — i.e., a rediscovery of the acquisition/asset-growth anomaly rather than the claimed conditional crowding-out effect.

This is the archived CashBurnPhysicalRDCrowding with the only change being DELTA(capx/at,1) swapped for TS_RANK(capx/at,5) — a cosmetic re-parameterization of an already-tested and weakly performing signal.

Using the goodwill stock (rather than R&D stock or capex level) as the conditioner on a PP&E-growth-versus-R&D-intensity tilt is a genuinely different pairing from KnowledgeOptionAbandonment and GoodwillMaintenanceNeglect, though the COALESCE(gdwl,0) zero mass will flatten a large fraction of the cross-section and should be watched in the portfolio diagnostics.
